verdict: REJECTED. The marginal public gain is NEGATIVE (-1.34e-06) before any df cost is charged, and adopting the base would move the empirical private estimate from 1.6469898 to 1.6470075, i.e. worse. 130 is unchanged.
what_this_settles: The anchor-recency defect is REAL at the base level: staleness costs 0.0022 per 36 days and 0.0071 per 96 days, measured monotonically with everything else held fixed. Extending training anchors from 342 to 378 removes a 66-day gap and should be worth roughly 0.004 standalone. It contributes NOTHING to the ensemble. The saturation, not the base quality, is binding.
three_independent_lines_now_agree: Perfect unregularised weighting of every measured base gives 1.6461003, still 0.0011 short of top-1.
Direct measurement of base-to-ensemble propagation gives a transfer coefficient of 0.21%.
A base carrying a genuine ~0.002-0.004 standalone improvement produces a marginal ensemble gain of -0.0000013.
conclusion: No single base, however much better, can move this ensemble. Our 29-base ridge is saturated with respect to the model family it is built from. Closing 0.001 would require a model that is different in kind, not better in degree.
actions: 130 remains the primary. No weights change.
EXEXT_decay runs stopped: they test the same refuted mechanism and would only tempt a second probe on a dead branch.
No further single-base search is justified by the evidence.
